Tom — hi, Rishi here from Infra. Below are concise answers and pointers; the attachments include a short runbook and a perf trace from a controlled noisy-neighbor test.

1) Noisy-neighbor mitigation (runtime level):
- Per-tenant runtime isolation: each tenant allocation runs in its own containerized runtime with CPU cgroups and isolated CUDA contexts; we avoid shared user-space processes between tenants.
- KV cache scoping: KV caches are materialized per-deployment/model instance and mounted into the runtime namespace. The runtime enforces per-tenant cache quotas and TTL-based eviction; caches are never shared across tenants.
- Request routing + dynamic throttles: our serving layer applies per-tenant request rate limits and continuous batching windows so a burst from one tenant triggers throttling rather than unbounded queue growth.
- Eviction policy: we implement LRU-based KV eviction with a prioritized token retention policy for request-critical prefixes. Eviction is deterministic and observable via our tracing hooks (see traces in noisy-neighbor-load-traces.zip).

2) Hardware partitioning (MIG support):
- We support NVIDIA MIG on compatible hardware. MIG is optional and can be requested per Dedicated pool; when enabled, MIG slices are pinned to tenant allocations so GPU compute and memory slices are hardware-partitioned. NOTE: MIG support depends on instance SKU; we document supported SKUs in the runbook.

3) Evidence artifacts:
- Attached: redwood_dedicated_isolation_runbook_v1.pdf — step-by-step tenant lifecycle, eviction cases, and observability checklist.
- Attached: mig-setup-snippets.txt — sample kube node config and device-plugin snippet used to carve MIG slices for tenant pools.
- Attached: noisy-neighbor-load-traces.zip — telemetry from a controlled test (two tenants, one generating synthetic worst-case throughput) showing request latencies, GPU utilization per slice, and KV eviction events over a 30-minute window.

Additional notes: our runtime enforces process and namespace separation; we run kernel-level mitigations for known GPU side-channels where applicable and keep up-to-date mitigations in the infra baseline. For customers that require stronger hardware isolation we recommend dedicated single-tenant nodes (no shared GPUs at all).

If you'd like, we can redact internal hostnames in the traces — let me know the format you prefer.
